title: Match words against a prefix with a composed BiPredicate

blocks.text: `BiPredicate<T, U>` tests two values together: `boolean test(T t, U u)`. It composes with `and()`, `or()` and `negate()`, like `Predicate`.

items: `startsWithAndLongerThan(int minLength)` returns a `BiPredicate<String, String>` that, for `(word, prefix)`, is true when the word is longer than `minLength` **and** starts with `prefix`. Build it from two BiPredicates joined with `and()`.
`matching(List<String> words, String prefix, BiPredicate<String, String> rule)` returns the words for which `rule.test(word, prefix)` is true, in order.

blocks.text: Check the page's example with prefix `"he"` against the words `hi, hello, hey, java, javafx`. A list may contain `null`, which no rule should ever be handed.

cases.says: Words that pass the rule, or its negation, are kept in order.
A word exactly minLength long is not longer than minLength, so it is left out.
A null word is skipped before any rule sees it, so even a negated rule never keeps it.

concepts: A BiPredicate tests two values together and composes with and, or and negate like a Predicate.
